verifier_note: Checked every warrant source by retrieval (WebFetch plus raw GitHub blob fetches when WebFetch's line-counting proved unreliable), every engine_note claim against si-rpg-engine's actual main branch (Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, lib.rs, rapier_law.rs, build.mjs, Cargo.lock via gh api), and ran the lane's own compile_oracle.py against the real pinned rustc 1.98.1 toolchain (33/33 checks pass, re-confirmed after the input file was regenerated mid-task with additional no_warnings/wasm_no_imports gates). I hand-reproduced two things beyond what checks[] covers: the entire crate-type cdylib-vs-rlib/tests/doctest mechanism in a toy crate (every claimed error code, warning, and exit code matched verbatim), and the canon_quat edge-case arithmetic, whose source proved byte-identical to GitHub main. Nothing was refuted. The one systemic weakness: recipe 2's headline claim (adding rlib changed the solver's actual wasm SHA-256) is an unreproduced empirical measurement on the real solver at a historical commit — I verified the mechanism is plausible and every surrounding claim reproduces exactly, but I could not re-derive that specific hash pair without checking out solver/ at e5fbcb9 outside the permitted scope, so it is marked plausible rather than solid. A second, minor weakness: that same recipe carries zero checks[] entries, meaning the non-model oracle has no automated coverage of it at all and every future edit to it will go unchecked unless someone adds checks by hand.
